short: Carbon distribution in multi-phase γ-TiAl based alloys and i
title: Carbon distribution in multi-phase γ-TiAl based alloys and its influence on mechanical properties and phase formation

lanes.label: Classical tools
lanes.sub: collapsed to one node per state

states.title: Hypothesis and design
states.head: How C partitions among gamma, alpha2 and beta_o in multi-phase TNM alloys, and its effect on phase hardness and phase formation, is unresolved. Add C to the beta-solidifying TNM alloy (TNM0.75C) and compare it with C-free TNM.

states.title: Structure state
states.head: C lowers the beta_o phase fraction and raises the alpha2 fraction. The reduced beta_o volume in TNM0.75C accommodates a higher Mo content.
states.detail: Absorbed: n7 (STR/phase/fraction), n9 (STR/chemistry/composition), n10 (STR/phase/identity), n13 (STR/chemistry/composition), n6 (STR/microstructure/shape). Premises: Schloffer et al.: pure beta_o 8.0 GPa; beta_o+omega_o 9.6-11.3 GPa depending on heat treatment; The beta_o/omega_o orientation relationship puts both spot sets in the <111>beta_o zone axis [53]

states.title: Property state and mechanisms
states.head: C strongly stabilises alpha/alpha2, switching TNM0.75C to peritectic solidification and a transformation path leaving less beta_o. Growing omega_o rejects Mo into beta_o; a higher Mo level in beta_o impedes or prevents omega_o formation.
states.detail: Absorbed: n8 (MEC/pathway), n11 (MEC/pathway), n12 (PRP/value), n15 (PRP/value), n17 (MEC/pathway). Premises: C is a strong alpha/alpha2 stabiliser in gamma-TiAl alloys [11,16]; omega_o in beta_o is depleted in group VIb elements (Mo [49], W [54]) by EDS; Interstitial solutes raise hardness by solid-solution hardening

states.title: Conclusion
states.head: C hardens gamma and alpha2 directly but softens beta_o indirectly: by cutting beta_o fraction it enriches beta_o in Mo and suppresses omega_o; C also segregates to interfaces
